title: Affine formal-map dictionary with natural section-limit comparisons
statement: Let X be affine Noetherian, J ideal sheaf data, H coherent, N a coherent formal module, and δ:N→completion(H) [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Put A=Γ(X,⊤), I=J(⊤), S=AdicCompletion I A, L=tilde [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] followed by chart pullback, and C=L followed by formal completion. Given P over A, ε:L(P)≅H and any η:C(P)≅C(S⊗P) [def-weil-module-base-change], there exist Q over S, an S-linear φ:Q→S⊗P, ρ:N≅C(Q restricted to A), and A-linear equivalences a:Q≅lim Γ(N_n) and b:S⊗P≅lim Γ(completion(H)_n). They satisfy δ=ρ followed by C(φ), η inverse, and completion(ε), and b(φ(x))=lim Γ(δ_n)(a(x)) for every x. No torsion assumption or annihilator conclusion is included.

source.place: Tags 087W, 00MA and 0889(1), affine representation and tensor comparison before applying Remark 0888

proof.text: Coherence implies quasi-coherence and finite type. The affine finite-generator theorem makes top sections finite. The natural section equivalence for restriction to Spec A and the tilde unit, applied to epsilon restricted along X.isoSpec.inv, identify P with those finite sections. Thus P is finite and B=S tensor P is a finite S-module.

Take the finite-module to formal-system equivalence E and its two natural comparisons beta and gamma. Put Q=E.inverse(N). Let c:E(Q) isomorphic to N be the counit. Put t=beta(B), then eta inverse, then completion(epsilon). Lift t to the coherent formal subcategory. Fullness of E gives psi:Q to B lifting c.hom followed by delta and t inverse. Its underlying S-linear map is phi. Set rho=c inverse followed by beta(Q). Naturality of beta and cancellation of c and t prove the formal-map factorization.

Define a as gamma(Q) followed by the actual section-limit map of c, and b as gamma(B) followed by the actual section-limit map of t. All maps are isomorphisms, giving A-linear equivalences. Naturality of gamma gives R(psi) followed by gamma(B) equals gamma(Q) followed by lim sections E(psi). Compose with lim sections t, replace E(psi) followed by t with c followed by delta, and use functoriality of the section-limit functor. Evaluating this equality of ModuleCat morphisms at x proves the square. This works for the given eta, without normalizing it to the tensor unit.

lean.statement:
theorem affine_formal_map_limit_dictionary
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsAffine X] (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (H : CoherentModules X) (N : CoherentFormalModule X J)
    (δ : N ⟶ (completion X J).obj H) :
    let A := Γ(X, ⊤)
    let I := J.ideal ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top X⟩
    let S := AdicCompletion I A
    let L := tilde.functor A ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pullback X.isoSpec.hom
    let C := L ⋙ formalCompletionFunctor J
    ∀ (P : ModuleCat.{u} A) (ε : L.obj P ≅ H.obj)
      (η : C.obj P ≅ C.obj (ModuleCat.of A (S ⊗[A] P))),
    ∃ Q : ModuleCat.{u} S,
      letI := Module.restrictScalars A S Q
      letI := IsScalarTower.restrictScalars A S Q
      ∃ (φ : Q →ₗ[S] S ⊗[A] P)
        (ρ : N.obj ≅ C.obj (ModuleCat.of A Q))
        (a : Q ≃ₗ[A] ↥(limit (N.obj ⋙
          SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op ⊤)) : ModuleCat A))
        (b : (S ⊗[A] P) ≃ₗ[A] ↥(limit (((completion X J).obj H).obj ⋙
          SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op ⊤)) : ModuleCat A)),
        δ.hom = ρ.hom ≫ C.map (ModuleCat.ofHom (φ.restrictScalars A)) ≫
          η.inv ≫ (formalCompletionFunctor J).map ε.hom ∧
        ∀ x : Q, b (φ x) =
          (lim.map (Functor.whiskerRight δ.hom
            (SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op ⊤)))).hom (a x)
